reviews.decision_reason: map_coverage preserves the upstream needs window and assigns direct coverage only when an exact need match exists in the supplied capabilities. The observed coverage correctly leaves n06-r01 and n06-r07 unsupported and marks the six matching needs direct.

prioritize_needs reverses the unsupported signal: it sets unsupported to true when coverage == 'direct'. This makes covered needs rank before genuinely unsupported needs and causes the top priority to become n06-r02 instead of the highest-ranked unsupported need n06-r01. This is the behaviorally significant root cause in the chain.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: Rank unsupported needs before covered needs
Use upstream provenance rank within each group
Preserve visible contradiction between coverage and unsupported fields

reviews.decision_reason: synthesize_recommendation retains the eight priority rows and constructs the recommendation from the first already-ranked priority. Its output is downstream of the bad ordering but the local transformation follows its declared role.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: Construct recommendation from first ranked record

reviews.decision_reason: select_demand_records keeps all supplied corpus rows because every demand_score is at least 3, with the fallback IDs also included. No source/output contradiction is visible for this boundary in the supplied package.
normalize_evidence preserves the bounded allowed-record window n06-r01 through n06-r08, applies JSON-safe sentinels, and keeps numeric fields normalized. No contradictory evidence is visible.

criteria_outcomes.criterion: Normalize required columns and missing values

reviews.decision_reason: assemble_provenance ranks normalized needs by descending demand_score with record_id as the tie-breaker, producing the supplied evidence-source ranks. This matches the upstream handoff used downstream.
